## What you need

| input | required | notes |
|---|---|---|
| DNA BAM | yes | coordinate sorted and indexed, GRCh38 / hg38 with `chr` names, the cell barcode in the `CB` tag; duplicates flagged or removed |
| cell whitelist | yes | one barcode per line (a trailing `-1` is stripped) |
| reference FASTA | yes | the FASTA the reads were aligned to (GC content per bin), with its `.fai` |
| phased heterozygous SNPs | for the allele channel; required in tumour mode | VCF with `GT` phased (`0|1`) and a `PS` phase-set tag, e.g. Clair3 + longphase, selected with `scphasedcn select-hets`; normal-tissue mode: preferably joined into chromosome-wide haplotypes with `scphasedcn hybrid-phase` (section 1) |
| sex | yes | `female` or `male` (chrX / chrY copy number) |
| cell metadata | no | cell types (normal tissue), cells known to be copy-number neutral, groups; see below |
| known events | no | regions reported as their own calls (e.g. a known trisomy; `name=chr:start-end`, 0-based half-open, an open end = the chromosome end); normal mode calls them per cell, in pools only with `pool_events` (off by default, experimental) |

The genome is hg38 only: the bundled chromosome sizes, ENCODE blacklist v2 and centromere coordinates are hg38, and
so are the chrX centromere and acrocentric arm defaults of the caller.

Reads: the extractor keeps primary, non-duplicate records with MAPQ >= 30 whose `CB` is in the whitelist; each record
is one fragment. SPLONGGET read names of the form `<CB>_#<uuid>_<sign><piece>of<npieces>` let it recognise pieces of
one raw read; other read names are accepted (each record is then its own read).

Whitelists in RNA-barcode space (10x Multiome GEX barcodes) are translated to the ATAC-space barcodes of the BAM with
`--barcode-map` (a TSV with columns `atac_barcode` and `rna_barcode`).

## 1. Phasing

The allele channel needs heterozygous SNPs phased within the sample. Call and phase them on the pooled reads of all
cells (the "pseudobulk" BAM); one recipe that works for ONT R10.4.1 data:

```bash
# 1. a clean BAM: primary, mapped, not duplicate, MAPQ >= 30
samtools view -@ 16 -b -F 0xd04 -q 30 -o sample.clean.bam sample.bam $(echo chr{1..22} chrX)
samtools index -@ 16 sample.clean.bam

# 2. Clair3 (docker://hkubal/clair3; pick the model of your basecaller, e.g. r1041_e82_400bps_sup_v520)
run_clair3.sh --bam_fn=sample.clean.bam --ref_fn=GRCh38.fa --threads=32 --platform=ont \
    --model_path=/models/r1041_e82_400bps_sup_v520 --ctg_name=$(echo chr{1..22} chrX | tr ' ' ',') \
    --sample_name=sample --output=clair3/

# 3. longphase on the PASS heterozygous biallelic SNVs
bcftools view -f PASS -v snps -m2 -M2 -g het -Oz -o pass_het.vcf.gz clair3/merge_output.vcf.gz
tabix -p vcf pass_het.vcf.gz
longphase phase -s pass_het.vcf.gz -b sample.clean.bam -r GRCh38.fa -o sample.longphase --ont -t 32
bgzip sample.longphase.vcf && tabix -p vcf sample.longphase.vcf.gz

# 4. select the sites the extractor uses
scphasedcn select-hets --vcf sample.longphase.vcf.gz --out het_phased.vcf.gz \
    --loci 1000G_snvs_hg38.vcf.gz --stats het_phased.select_stats.tsv
```

`select-hets` keeps PASS biallelic heterozygous SNVs with GQ >= 10 and DP between 20 and the 99th percentile of the
candidates (collapsed repeats have excess depth). There is deliberately no allele-frequency window: it would remove
sites in regions of LOH or amplification in tumours. `--loci` (recommended) intersects the sites with a population
SNV panel, e.g. the 1000 Genomes sites on GRCh38 (position, REF and ALT must match), which removes most systematic
long-read genotyping errors; chrX is kept without the intersect by default (`--no-loci-contigs`).

longphase phase blocks (typically tens to a few hundred kb) are not oriented relative to each other. What the caller
needs on top of them depends on the mode.

**Normal tissue: chromosome-scale haplotypes are recommended.** With blocks alone, `call_scn()` orients each block
of a cell by the pseudobulk of the other cells (`loo`). The orientation of a block is then set by the majority of the
cells, so an event carried by few cells is averaged away (its oriented allele fraction stays near 0.5), and allelic
bias shared by all cells (germline copy-number variants, mapping bias, X inactivation) is aligned the same way in
every cell, which produces false per-cell events. In one normal-tissue sample, per-cell events on the autosomes fell
from 258 to 129 when the same sample was phased with the recipe below. Join the blocks with a population
(reference-panel) phase of the same sample's genotypes (what this does for per-cell losses and copy-neutral LOH is
limited by the population phase's switch errors; see the limits below):

```bash
# 5. population phasing of the sample's heterozygous SNVs, one chromosome at a time (here Beagle 5 with the
#    1000 Genomes GRCh38 panel and its genetic maps; SHAPEIT works as well). The panel's contig names must match
#    the VCF's; impute=false keeps the output to the sample's own sites.
for c in $(echo chr{1..22} chrX); do
  java -jar beagle.jar gt=pass_het.vcf.gz ref=panel/1kGP_${c}.vcf.gz map=maps/${c}.GRCh38.map \
      chrom=${c} impute=false nthreads=8 out=popphased_${c}
  tabix -p vcf popphased_${c}.vcf.gz
done

# 6. orient the longphase blocks by the population phase: one phase set per chromosome
scphasedcn hybrid-phase --blocks het_phased.vcf.gz --population 'popphased_{chrom}.vcf.gz' \
    --out het_hybrid.vcf.gz --block-tsv hybrid_blocks.tsv --chrom-tsv hybrid_chroms.tsv
```

and extract with the hybrid VCF (`--snps het_hybrid.vcf.gz --phased`, section 2). `hybrid-phase` lets every
heterozygous SNV that both files phase (same REF / ALT; imputed markers excluded) vote on its block's orientation,
flips the blocks whose majority disagrees with the population phase and gives all oriented blocks one phase set per
chromosome; blocks without votes or with a tie keep their own phase set. `call_scn()` then sums the votes per region
(`chromosome` orientation). It warns in normal mode when the allele features were oriented `loo` on block phasing,
and `cell_features()` notes chromosomes whose phasing differs from the rest (e.g. chrX left in blocks when the panel
has no chrX; the unoriented blocks of such a chromosome are summed as they are, so its allele channel carries little
or no signal).

**Tumour mode keeps the block-only recipe (steps 1-4).** It orients each block by the pseudobulk of the cell's clone,
which is the right reference for events shared by a clone, and it does not need the population phase: the junction
flips of statistical phasing (below) would only add switch errors that the clone orientation has to undo.

Limits:

- Statistical phasing flips a fraction of the block junctions (switch errors). A flipped block puts its votes on the
  wrong haplotype in every cell, so the oriented allele fraction of a real event moves towards 0.5. Normal mode
  scores losses and copy-neutral LOH at a major-haplotype fraction of 0.98; at an attenuated fraction a gain state
  can fit better, and the event is not called. In simulations, per-cell recall of an arm loss fell from 1.00 without
  switch errors to 0.88, 0.65 and 0.00 with a switch error every 20, 10 and 2 Mb, with a large spread between
  simulated genomes. Copy-neutral LOH, which has no depth signal, fell further (0.53 and 0.00 at 20 and 10 Mb):
  losses with a clear depth shift (whole chromosomes, large losses) are less affected than copy-neutral events, but
  not immune. Per-cell recall of losses and copy-neutral LOH on hybrid phasing therefore depends on the switch-error
  rate of the population phase and has not been validated on real data. An attenuation-aware state set exists as an
  opt-in (caller parameter `normal_states: "normal_att"`, or `"auto"` to use it whenever the phasing regime is
  chromosome-scale; the grid `f_att_normal`, by default 0.70, 0.80, 0.90 and 0.98): it scores losses and copy-neutral
  LOH also at attenuated fractions, so that attenuated events keep their label. It trades recall of attenuated
  losses and copy-neutral LOH against more false loss / copy-neutral LOH labels on cells without events and some
  recall of gains (its lower fractions overlap the 2:1 and 3:1 gain fractions, so weak gains can be labelled
  copy-neutral LOH); the total number of calls stays at the null budget. It is not the default: the right grid
  depends on the switch-error rate of the population phase and has not been benchmarked on real data. The `--chrom-tsv` report gives, per chromosome, how often the population phase disagrees with the
  reads inside blocks (`switch_rate`, `minority_frac`).
- With blocks alone, only events shared by several percent of the cells are visible in the allele channel. The depth
  channel does not depend on phasing.

## 2. Extraction (`scphasedcn`)

```bash
# normal tissue: the hybrid VCF of step 6; tumour: het_phased.vcf.gz of step 4
scphasedcn run --bam sample.bam --barcodes barcodes.tsv.gz --fasta GRCh38.fa \
    --snps het_hybrid.vcf.gz --phased --out results/sample/extract --jobs 8
```

`run` extracts every chromosome in parallel (`--jobs`; a deep chromosome takes a few GB of memory) and merges. On a
cluster, run `scphasedcn extract --chrom <chrom>` as one job per chromosome and `scphasedcn merge` after them, with the
same options. A sample yaml keeps the paths in one place (`--config sample.yaml --sample <key>`, also read by the
caller's command line):

```{r template, comment = ""}
cat(readLines(system.file("extdata", "sample_template.yaml", package = "scphasedcn")), sep = "\n")
```

Reference files: the FASTA is required. The blacklist, centromeres and chromosome sizes default to the bundled hg38
tables; a tandem-repeat BED (`--trf`) is optional (it adds the repeat fraction of each bin, used by the bin filter).

## 3. The extraction directory

`call_scn(dir)` reads three files of the directory:

- `bins_100kb.h5ad` (AnnData): `X` = clean fragments per cell (rows) x 100 kb bin (columns). `var` per bin: `chrom`,
  `start`, `end` (0-based, half-open), `gc`, `frac_blacklist`, `frac_trf`, `is_centromere`, `peak_bp`. `obs` per cell:
  the QC counts below.
- `fragments.tsv.gz` + `.tbi` (bgzipped, tabix-indexed, one header line starting with `#`): one row per fragment
  with columns `chrom, start, end, cell, strand, mapq, flags, len, piece, npieces, hap, nsnp, ps, read_id`. `hap` is
  the fragment's haplotype from the phased SNPs it covers (0 none, 1 haplotype A, 2 haplotype B, 3 ambiguous) and `ps`
  the phase set of its first phased SNP (-1 none). The caller collapses a cell's fragments closer than `mol_gap`
  (2 kb) into one molecule with one vote.
- `cells_qc.tsv`: per cell `n_pass` (passing records), `n_clean` (outside the blacklist), `frac_mapq60`, `frac_chrM`,
  ... The caller's cell QC (`cell_qc()`) keeps cells with at least 5,000 clean fragments, at least half of them at
  MAPQ 60 and at most 20 % on chrM.

Also written: `alleles_dna.h5ad` (allele counts per cell x SNP), `summary.json`, and `partials/` (the per-chromosome
pieces).

The package's simulator writes the same layout:

```{r layout}
library(scphasedcn)
sim = simulate_scn(n_cells = 40, seed = 1)
d = file.path(tempdir(), "sim_extract")
invisible(write_sim_dataset(sim, d))
b = read_bins_h5ad(file.path(d, "bins_100kb.h5ad"))
dim(b$counts)
head(b$bins)
head(read_fragments(file.path(d, "fragments.tsv.gz")))
```

## 4. Cell metadata

Everything here is optional. `make_cell_meta()` builds the table (`--cell-meta` of the command line) from the
extractor's `cells_qc.tsv` and your labels:

- `cell_type`: cell types from an RNA (or ATAC) annotation of the same barcodes. Normal-tissue mode builds the depth
  reference of a cell from the other cells of its type, which removes cell-type chromatin effects on read depth;
  without cell types, all cells form one reference.
- `flat`: cells known to be copy-number neutral (e.g. from a matched assay). Normal-tissue mode uses them as its null
  cells with `null_cells = "features"`; without them use `null_cells = "select"` (the caller selects null cells from
  the data). Tumour mode fits its input depth and allelic null on them; its normal reference pool is the normal clone
  the caller finds and cleans itself, not these cells.
- `group`: tumour mode, groups whose pseudobulk orients the phase blocks (`groups = "group"`), e.g. spatial regions
  or RNA clusters.

```{r meta}
qc = data.table::fread(file.path(d, "cells_qc.tsv"))
types = data.table::data.table(cell = qc$cell, cell_type = sim$scn$cells$cell_type)
m = make_cell_meta(file.path(d, "cells_qc.tsv"), cell_types = types)
head(m)
data.table::fwrite(m, file.path(tempdir(), "cell_meta.tsv"), sep = "\t")
```

Multiplets (barcodes holding more than one nucleus) inflate calls; pass a per-cell multiplet probability as
`multiplets` (a table `cell, prob`) to leave them out of the null and the clone discovery.
